patients.summary: Software developer with long-standing type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and class II obesity who joins in 2021. Adds an unexplained hyperzincemia, metabolic syndrome, obesity hypoventilation with obstructive sleep apnea, and an ED gout flare after his last practice visit.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is 52, wants a new primary care doctor. Previous office is closing its adult panel at the end of the year. Has diabetes and blood pressure, on 4 meds, says he is 'behind on everything.' Membership info emailed. New patient slot booked 9/14 at 8:20. Records release form sent for his prior office, he will sign and return.

Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
52M here to establish. Prior PCP office is closing its adult panel.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes for about 7 years, by his own description never well controlled. Admits he takes the metformin 'most days,' sometimes forgets the evening dose, and that his diet is heavy on carbs and takeout during deadline weeks. No polyuria or polydipsia right now. No vision change, no foot numbness. HTN and cholesterol on meds for several years. Weight has crept up since he went fully remote.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, HCTZ 25 daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: none.
FHx: father T2DM and HTN; mother high cholesterol and obesity; paternal grandfather MI at 62.
SHx: married. Software developer, desk all day. Never smoked. 3-4 beers most evenings after work. No regular exercise.
Screening: colonoscopy 2019 at prior office, he believes normal. Two Pfizer doses this spring.

Exam: obese, comfortable. BP as recorded. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, obese, nontender. No leg edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament and vibration intact, DP pulses 2+.
PHQ-2 negative.

A/P:
1. T2DM, likely above goal. A1c, CMP, UACR today. Reviewed adherence; pillbox suggested. Continue metformin.
2. HTN, near goal in office. Continue lisinopril and HCTZ.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
4. Obesity class II. Talked about the beer as a big calorie source; he is not ready to cut back yet.
5. Health maintenance: flu shot today. HCV and HIV screening today, he agrees. Prior records requested.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kurt, your labs are back. Kidney and liver tests are fine, blood count normal, urine protein normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Your A1c is 8.0, which is above where we want it (under 7). Triglycerides are high too, and both of those move with sugar, beer and weight. Let's see what a few months of taking the metformin every day does before we talk about adding anything. See you in December.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: 38 pages received by fax from the patient's former primary care office, covering 2015 to 2021. Includes problem list (type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity), medication list matching current meds, A1c values mostly between 7.5 and 8.5, and a screening colonoscopy report dated 05/2019: complete to cecum, good prep, no polyps, repeat in 10 years. No allergies listed. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Prior records reviewed. Long history of A1c in the high 7s to mid 8s on metformin alone, no other agents ever tried per notes. Colonoscopy 2019 normal, next due 2029. Nothing else actionable. Health maintenance updated.

documents.title: Outside immunization report
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Retail pharmacy reported a Pfizer COVID booster given 11/6/2021. Entered into immunization history.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back for diabetes and BP check. Says he has been better about the evening metformin, maybe 5 nights out of 7. Diet unchanged; holiday season at work means pizza in the office. Still having beers most nights. No hypoglycemia symptoms, no GI upset on metformin.
O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular. No edema.
POC A1c 7.9.
A/P: T2DM still above goal, barely moved. Options discussed including a second agent; he wants one more round of trying on his own first. Continue current regimen. Recheck at physical in spring with lipids. HTN fine today. Refills x 90 days with 3 refills sent.

documents.title: Question about checking sugars
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it worth me getting a glucose meter to check at home? Old doctor never had me do it.

documents.title: RE: Question about checking sugars
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: On metformin alone, routine fingersticks don't add much and your A1c tells us what we need. If we add a medicine later that can cause lows, we'll set you up with one then.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic request from patient's pharmacy for 90-day fills of atorvastatin 40 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. Last visit 12/14/21. Approved under refill protocol, 90 days x 1 refill.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53-year-old man for his yearly exam. Feels fine, no complaints. Honest that he has been inconsistent with both the diet and the pills since winter; some weeks good, some not.

ROS otherwise negative: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no urinary symptoms, no bowel change.
Meds unchanged (metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40 qhs, HCTZ 25). NKDA.
Social unchanged; still 3-4 beers most evenings.

Exam: BP 138/86. BMI 33. Well appearing. Eyes and ears normal. Neck without nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft, no masses. Extremities without edema. Feet: no ulcers or calluses, monofilament intact both sides, pulses good. Skin without concerning lesions.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Annual exam. Shingrix #1 and PCV20 today. Colonoscopy current to 2029. Eye exam this year, he will book.
2. T2DM, adherence uneven. A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today.
3. Lipids with labs today.
4. HTN at goal-ish, continue.
5. Weight and alcohol: same conversation as before.
Will message results.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with physical labs. Triglycerides 650, total 210, LDL 130, HDL 35. A1c remains well above goal. Kidney function and urine protein normal, liver tests normal. Zinc level 141, high; reference 60-120. Asked about supplements, multivitamins, zinc lozenges, denture cream, work exposures: none, he works from home. Will repeat zinc with his second Shingrix in June to confirm before calling it anything.
Given triglycerides this high plus persistent A1c, offered endocrinology input; he agrees. Referral placed. Reinforced cutting back alcohol, which drives the triglycerides.
Added hyperzincemia to problem list pending recheck.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for second Shingrix, given L deltoid, tolerated. Reports a sore arm and a low-energy day after dose 1, nothing more. Blood drawn for repeat zinc level per PCP order, fasting not required. Reminded about the endocrinology appointment on 7/20; he has it on his calendar.

documents.title: Zinc recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kurt, the repeat zinc came back at 137, still a little above the normal range (60-120), so the first result was not a lab fluke. You told me you don't take any multivitamin, lozenges or supplements, and nothing on your medication list explains it. It is not causing any problem we can see. I'd like to keep an eye on it with your yearly blood work rather than chase it further right now. Let me know if you start any supplements.

documents.title: RE: Zinc recheck
documents.author: patient
documents.body: OK thanks. Nope, nothing like that, I don't even take vitamin D. Should I avoid anything?

documents.title: RE: Zinc recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No restrictions. Just skip zinc lozenges and cold remedies with zinc if you get a cold.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY GROUP — CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of service: 07/20/2022
Referred by: primary care physician
Reason: diabetes above goal, hypertriglyceridemia

Thank you for sending Mr. Blanchard, a 53-year-old software developer with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and obesity. Since his visit with you in April he has noticed being thirsty a lot more, getting up to urinate, and he has lost about 10 pounds over the last two months without trying.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Social: sedentary desk job; beer most evenings.
Family: father with diabetes and hypertension, mother with high cholesterol and obesity, paternal grandfather MI at 62.

Exam: BP 145/92. BMI 32. Waist circumference 102 cm. Acanthosis nigricans along the posterior neck. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart and lungs normal. Feet with intact sensation.

Fasting labs: glucose 132 mg/dL, hemoglobin A1c 7.2%, total cholesterol 220, HDL 35, triglycerides 250, LDL (calculated) 140.

Impression:
1. Type 2 diabetes with insulin resistance; symptoms of hyperglycemia recently, A1c 7.2 today.
2. Metabolic syndrome: waist, triglycerides, low HDL, blood pressure and glucose all meet criteria.
3. Hypertriglyceridemia, improved from the 650 you saw in April.

Recommendations: We spent most of the visit on diet. Cutting the daily beer and refined carbohydrates is the single biggest lever on both his sugars and triglycerides, and he seemed receptive. No medication changes for now; continue metformin, statin and his blood pressure medicines. Follow-up with primary care; happy to see him again if A1c stays above goal.

Outside Endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got the endocrinologist's letter. A1c 7.2, which is better than spring. She agrees with no new meds for now and put a lot of weight on cutting back the beer and carbs. I'd like to recheck your A1c and fasting sugar around the new year. We'll set up a visit in early January.

documents.title: RE: Endocrinology letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sounds good. I'm down to weekends only on the beer for now. We'll see how long that lasts lol.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine DM visit. Nothing major going on. Main thing he brings up is feeling more tired than usual for the past few months, worse late afternoon; sleeping through the night as far as he knows, works long screen days. The thirst and night urination he had in the summer are gone. No weight loss now, has actually gained a few pounds back over the holidays. Beer back to most nights since Thanksgiving, he admits.

Vitals: BP 138/86, P 76. BMI about 33.
Gen: well, obese, central distribution. No acanthosis seen on the neck today. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. Feet intact.

Labs from 12/29: fasting glucose 132, A1c 6.8 (best number we have on him).

A/P:
1. T2DM, A1c 6.8, at goal. Continue metformin 1000 BID. Credit to the summer diet changes.
2. Fatigue, nonspecific; sugars are better, not a hyperglycemia picture. Sleep hygiene and screen time discussed. Revisit at next visit if it persists.
3. HTN 138/86, continue.
4. Hyperzincemia, followed, next level with summer labs.
RTC 6 months with fasting labs.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: abdomen bigger, tired.

54M with T2DM, HTN, hyperlipidemia, obesity. Drew labs at 8 before the visit. Says his waistband has gone up a size since spring and he is dragging most afternoons. Asked directly about alcohol: back to 3-4 beers on most nights after work, plus a lot of bread, pasta and fried takeout. Denies chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea. No abdominal pain, no jaundice, no change in stool color. No leg swelling.

BP 138/86. BMI about 34.
Gen: obese, NAD. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen: protuberant, soft, nontender; liver edge palpable a little below the costal margin, smooth, nontender. No spleen tip. No ascites appreciated. Ext: no edema.
PHQ-2: 1.

Labs this morning: A1c 7.8 (up from 6.8). Lipids: total 220, HDL 35, LDL 130, TG 480. CMP: liver tests and kidney function normal. Zinc pending.

A/P:
1. T2DM, worse, tracks with the return to daily beer and diet. He wants to get back to what worked last summer before adding a medicine. Continue metformin.
2. Mild hepatomegaly on exam, liver tests normal. Alcohol and weight discussed plainly. He set a goal of no beer on weeknights.
3. Hypertriglyceridemia / hyperlipidemia, continue atorvastatin 40.
4. Fatigue and girth, as above.
5. HTN, continue.
6. Hyperzincemia, level pending.
RTC 6 months. Physical overdue; front desk to book.

documents.author: PCP

documents.body: Optometry report, dilated exam 11/28/2023. Best corrected acuity 20/20 right, 20/25 left. Pressures normal. Lens clear. Retina: no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization either eye; no diabetic retinopathy. Return in one year.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

O: Vitals as charted, weight up again. Heart and lungs normal. No edema. Monofilament intact.
A1c today 7.6. BMP normal, potassium normal on HCTZ.
A/P: T2DM above goal. Offered adding a second agent again, discussed options and their weight effects; he would like to wait until the physical and try once more. I will hold him to it. HTN stable. Physical booked for May with full labs.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 55M.

Interval: no ED visits. Raises something new: he is sleepy all day, nodding off in afternoon standups, and wakes several mornings a week with a dull headache that wears off by mid-morning. Has been going on and building over several months. No vision change, no weakness, no vomiting.

Meds unchanged: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40 qhs, HCTZ 25. NKDA. Beer still most nights.

Exam: vitals as charted. Obese, alert. Oropharynx clear. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No leg edema. Feet: sensation intact, pulses good. Skin ok.
PHQ-2 1.

A/P:
1. Annual. Colonoscopy due 2029. Vaccines current. Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UACR.
2. Daytime sleepiness and morning headaches in a man with his habitus and neck: worry is a sleep-related breathing problem. Referred to pulmonology for evaluation and a sleep study.
3. T2DM: decide on second agent once A1c back.
4. HTN, hyperlipidemia: continue.
Return after pulmonology.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Results from Tuesday: A1c 7.5, not where we want it but slightly better than February. Cholesterol numbers about the same as last year, triglycerides still high. Kidney, liver and urine protein normal. Blood count fine. The pulmonology office should call you within two weeks; let us know if they don't.

documents.title: RE: Physical results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: They called already, July 17 was the first opening. Thanks.

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood
Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: Technically adequate study, body habitus limits some windows. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness and normal systolic function, estimated ejection fraction 55-60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricular free wall is thickened, consistent with right ventricular hypertrophy. Atria normal in size. Aortic, mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. Aortic root normal.
reports.conclusion: Right ventricular hypertrophy. Normal left ventricular size and function.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY AND SLEEP MEDICINE — NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Visit date: 07/17/2024
Referral source: primary care

The patient is a 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and class II obesity seen for daytime sleepiness and morning headaches. He drifts off during meetings and when sitting still in the afternoon; headaches are present on waking and fade over the morning.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, HCTZ 25 mg. No known drug allergies. Never smoker. Drinks beer most evenings. Works as a software developer.

Examination: BP 145/90, HR 88, RR 18. BMI 35. Large neck circumference. Lungs clear to auscultation. Regular heart rhythm. Pitting edema of both lower legs.

Data:
Arterial blood gas on room air: pH 7.43, PaCO2 55, PaO2 68, HCO3 32.
CBC: hemoglobin 18.5, hematocrit 55%.
Transthoracic echocardiogram today: right ventricular hypertrophy; LV normal.

Assessment: Daytime hypercapnia with a compensated pH and elevated bicarbonate in a patient with obesity, without lung disease to explain it, fits obesity hypoventilation syndrome. The elevated hemoglobin and right ventricular hypertrophy are in keeping with chronic hypoventilation.

Plan: Attended in-lab polysomnography to look for coexisting obstructive sleep apnea and guide positive airway pressure. Weight loss counseling. Advised avoiding alcohol in the evening and sedating medications. Return after the study.

Outside Pulmonary and Sleep Medicine

documents.title: Pulmonology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kurt, I received the pulmonologist's letter. The blood gas showed your carbon dioxide runs high, which is what they call obesity hypoventilation: breathing isn't fully keeping up, mostly at night. That fits the sleepiness and the morning headaches. Your red blood count is up and the heart ultrasound showed the right side of the heart working harder, both from the same problem. The sleep study they ordered is the next step, and treatment usually is a mask machine at night. Please do get the sleep study scheduled. Cutting the evening beer helps here too.

documents.title: RE: Pulmonology letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wow ok, that explains a lot. Sleep lab's first slot is December, I'm on a cancellation list.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, 56M.

Interval: had the overnight sleep study in December and saw pulmonology again in early January. He says they told him he has obstructive sleep apnea on top of the hypoventilation and set him up with a CPAP machine; has been using it most nights since early February. Sleepier days are a bit better, fewer morning headaches, though he takes the mask off some nights. We have not received a letter or the study report.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40 qhs, HCTZ 25. NKDA. Beer about 2 a night.

Exam: vitals as charted. Obese. Thick neck. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Trace pitting edema at both ankles. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable. Skin unremarkable.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Annual. Vaccines up to date for now; colonoscopy 2029. Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UACR, zinc.
2. OHS with sleep apnea per patient, on CPAP. Records request sent to pulmonology today so the chart has the study.
3. T2DM: A1c pending. If still above 7, start the second-agent conversation in earnest.
4. HTN, hyperlipidemia: continue.
5. Hyperzincemia: level today.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kurt, labs from Tuesday. A1c 7.3. Zinc is back up to 144 after being normal in 2023, so this comes and goes; still no symptoms or obvious cause, and I'll keep checking it yearly. Triglycerides remain high and the LDL is about where it has been. Red blood count still on the high side, which is what pulmonology expected with the breathing problem. Kidneys and urine protein fine. Keep using the CPAP every night; that matters for the blood count too.

documents.title: Records follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called pulmonology office re: records request faxed 3/11, nothing received. They had no request on file. Re-faxed release with cover sheet asking for 1/3/25 visit note and polysomnography report. Confirmed receipt by phone.

conditions.label: Severe obesity due to excess calories

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood
Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: Attended overnight in-laboratory diagnostic polysomnogram. Recording montage included EEG, EOG, chin and leg EMG, ECG, nasal pressure, oronasal thermistor, thoracic and abdominal effort belts and pulse oximetry. Sleep onset and architecture recorded; total sleep time adequate for interpretation. Respiratory events were predominantly obstructive apneas and hypopneas. Apnea-hypopnea index 25 events per hour. No central apnea pattern. Sinus rhythm on single-lead ECG. No periodic limb movement disorder.
PA and lateral views. Lungs clear. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size within normal limits for technique. Mediastinal contours normal. Bones intact.

Full pulmonary function testing with spirometry, lung volumes and pre/post bronchodilator. Good effort and reproducibility. FEV1 and FVC proportionally reduced with a preserved FEV1/FVC ratio. Total lung capacity mildly reduced. No significant response to bronchodilator.
reports.conclusion: Mild restrictive pattern without significant bronchodilator reversibility.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY AND SLEEP MEDICINE — FOLLOW-UP NOTE
Visit date: 01/03/2025

Returns after his sleep study. Daytime sleepiness and morning headaches are worse than in July, and he now has trouble holding concentration at work. His wife reports loud snoring and that he sometimes gasps in his sleep.

Medications unchanged: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide. NKDA.

Exam: BP 145/92, HR 88. BMI 36. Neck circumference 44 cm. Lungs clear. Pitting edema of the lower legs.

Arterial blood gas, room air: pH 7.32, PaCO2 58, PaO2 68, HCO3 29.
Chest x-ray today: unremarkable.
Pulmonary function tests today: mild restriction, no significant reversibility after bronchodilator.
Polysomnography 12/10/2024: obstructive sleep apnea, AHI 25 events/hour.

Assessment:
1. Obesity hypoventilation syndrome with coexisting obstructive sleep apnea. The mild restriction on PFTs is consistent with body habitus; no airway disease.
2. Severe obesity due to excess calories (BMI 36 with hypoventilation).

Plan: Start CPAP, auto-titrating 5 to 15 cm H2O, with a full-face mask; order sent to the durable medical equipment supplier. Download review at the next visit, and we will move to bilevel if hypercapnia does not improve. Weight loss and avoiding evening alcohol encouraged. No driving when drowsy.

Outside Pulmonary and Sleep Medicine

[Received 04/22/2025 after second request. Includes polysomnography report.]

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pulmonology note from January and the December PSG reviewed. OSA, AHI 25, with OHS. CPAP auto 5-15 started by pulmonology. Problem list updated with OSA and severe obesity. Patient told me in March he is using it most nights.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt in his home office, consented to video.
How he's doing: using CPAP nearly every night now, the machine app shows good hours. Days much more awake, headaches mostly gone. Saw pulmonology for a download check in the spring per him. Home BP cuff readings he reads to me run 130s/80s. No home glucose meter use. Beer 1-2 most nights.
No chest pain, no dyspnea.
A/P: T2DM, last A1c 7.3. Discussed adding a second medicine once more; he would prefer to see the A1c on CPAP and less alcohol first. Labs with fall visit. HTN, home readings acceptable. OHS/OSA, doing better on CPAP. Flu shot in October.

Doesn't go anywhere, stops a few minutes after he stops moving. Never at rest. No change in how far he can walk otherwise. No palpitations, no shortness of breath beyond baseline. CPAP going well.

ECG in office: NSR, normal.

1. Exertional chest discomfort, relieved with rest, in a 56-year-old with diabetes, hypertension, lipids and a grandfather with an early MI. Resting ECG normal. Referred to cardiology for evaluation. Reviewed reasons to call 911 (pain at rest, lasting over 15 minutes, with sweating or breathlessness).
2. T2DM: labs to be drawn with cardiology or at next visit.
3. Continue all current meds.

documents.title: Cardiology appointment
documents.author: patient

documents.title: RE: Cardiology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's reasonable as long as it stays the way you described: only with real exertion, mild, and gone within a few minutes of resting. If it happens at rest, lasts longer, or comes with sweating or shortness of breath, call 911. Ask to be put on their cancellation list.

documents.title: Went to the ER Saturday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Heads up, I ended up in the ER Saturday with my right big toe. Woke up Friday night and it was on fire, couldn't put any weight on it. This was two days after a wedding, a lot of beer and a steak. They stuck a needle in the joint and said it's gout. Gave me colchicine. Already a lot better this morning. Do I need to do anything?

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER Saturday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry to hear it, glad it's settling. Take the colchicine exactly as the ER wrote it, and stop it if you get diarrhea. Plenty of water, and go easy on beer for now. We'll request the ER records and go over gout prevention at your September visit. If the pain comes back or you get a fever, call us.

documents.title: Emergency Department Summary
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE — outside hospital
Date of service: 07/11/2026

Chief complaint: right great toe pain.

HPI: 57-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and class II obesity. Right big toe pain started suddenly the night before arrival and has escalated so he cannot bear weight. Two days ago he was at a wedding, drank heavily and had steak. No trauma. First episode.

PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, obesity, obesity hypoventilation syndrome, hyperzincemia.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime, hydrochlorothiazide.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, 3-4 beers daily.

Exam: Temp 37.8 C. Right first metatarsophalangeal joint red, swollen and exquisitely tender; limited by pain. Remainder of the foot without wounds. Other joints normal.

Procedure: right first MTP arthrocentesis under sterile technique, small volume of cloudy fluid obtained. Tolerated well.

Results: uric acid 8.5 mg/dL, WBC 11,000, CRP 20 mg/L, ESR 45 mm/hr. Synovial fluid polarized microscopy: negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals.

Diagnosis: acute gouty arthritis of the right first MTP (podagra).

Disposition: discharged home. Colchicine 0.6 mg tablets: 1.2 mg now, 0.6 mg one hour later, then 0.6 mg twice daily until the flare resolves. Avoid alcohol and large meat meals. Hydrochlorothiazide can raise uric acid; follow up with primary care in 1 to 2 weeks to review.

[Received 08/04/2026 after records request.]
